title: Sótano de las Golondrinas vs. Sótano de las Huahuas: Which One Should You Visit in 2026?
metaTitle: Sótano de las Golondrinas vs. Huahuas: Which to Visit?
metaDescription: Sótano de las Golondrinas (Cave of Swallows) vs. Sótano de las Huahuas: prices, how to get there, what it's really like and which one fits your trip.
excerpt: Cave of Swallows or the quieter Sótano de las Huahuas? Prices, bird-flight times, access from Ciudad Valles and Xilitla, and which sinkhole suits your kind of trip.
contentHtml:
The Sótano de las Golondrinas (Cave of Swallows) is one of the largest vertical shafts in the world open to the public, with a 376-meter free fall (up to 512 meters total depth), located in Aquismón, San Luis Potosí, a municipality tucked into the Sierra Madre Oriental less than two hours from Ciudad Valles. Every morning, thousands of white-collared swifts (Streptoprocne zonaris) spiral up out of it in one of the most impressive natural spectacles in Mexico. The most common question among travelers planning a trip through the Huasteca Potosina is whether it's more worth visiting than its lesser-known neighbor, the Sótano de las Huahuas. They aren't interchangeable: each one offers a completely different experience, and picking the wrong one can mean missing the birds' flight or showing up with no guide available.

In this side-by-side guide you'll find everything you need to decide with real information: updated prices, hours, distances from Ciudad Valles, which type of traveler each one suits and what to expect from each abyss in 2026. The Sótano de las Golondrinas is one of the most in-demand destinations in the entire Huasteca Potosina. The Sótano de las Huahuas, on the other hand, gets significantly fewer visitors, which guarantees a more intimate experience but takes more planning on your own.

At huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators across the region. This guide is updated with the real experiences of people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: September 2026. If you already know what you want to see, book your guided tour in the Huasteca Potosina now.

Sótano de las Golondrinas: what to see, how it works and why it's unique

What makes the Sótano de las Golondrinas so special?

The Sótano de las Golondrinas isn't a horizontal cave: it's an elliptical shaft that opens at the surface with a mouth roughly 60 meters across and widens to 300 meters at its broadest point before reaching the bottom at a depth of 512 meters. The show happens every dawn, when the birds spiral upward out of the shaft, and at dusk, when they come back in a vertical dive. In 2026, admission to the Sótano de las Golondrinas is $100 MXN per person. It isn't part of our tours: the Tamul Expedition ends at the Sótano de las Huahuas.

The groups we coordinate every season agree that the most powerful part of the experience isn't the view from the rim but the sound: the combined wingbeats of thousands of birds create a vibration you feel in your chest before you can even see them. Reaching the edge of the shaft in total darkness and waiting for the first streak of light is something travelers often describe as life-changing. A headlamp and warm clothes are a must, since temperatures near the rim can be 8–10°C lower than in town.

When the birds fly: exactly when to arrive

The site opens at 4:00 a.m. and closes at 6:00 p.m. every day of the year. The birds fly out around 5:00 a.m. in summer and around 6:00 a.m. in winter. The trail from the ejido's parking lot (an ejido is a community that owns the land) to the rim of the shaft takes about 20 minutes at a normal pace, so reaching the trailhead before 4:20 a.m. is essential if you don't want to rush in the dark. If it rains or the overnight temperature drops too low, the birds don't come out that day, which makes weather the biggest risk factor of the visit. We recommend reaching the rim at least 40 minutes before the expected flight time so you can get into position and let your eyes adjust to the dark.

To plan your time in the area, see our complete guide to the Sótano de las Golondrinas, with information on nesting season and the months with the most birds.

Sótano de las Huahuas: what it's like, how to get there and how it differs from the Sótano de las Golondrinas

What is the Sótano de las Huahuas, and who is it for?

The Sótano de las Huahuas is a vertical shaft also located in the Aquismón area. It's less well known and has a considerably smaller diameter, but it's just as impressive for anyone looking for a setting without crowds. First-time visitors are often surprised by the depth of the silence and by the vegetation around the rim: tree ferns, bromeliads and orchids grow on the limestone walls just a few meters from the opening. The Sótano de las Huahuas is also home to bird colonies, though in smaller numbers, and visiting it means coordinating directly with local guides from the ejido, since tourist infrastructure is minimal compared with the Sótano de las Golondrinas. See available tours in the Huasteca Potosina: the Tamul Expedition ends at the Sótano de las Huahuas.

An honest warning: access to the Sótano de las Huahuas can become impractical after heavy rain, because the dirt road gets slippery and is sometimes impassable for regular cars. If you're traveling between June and September, the rainy season in the Huasteca Potosina can close access without notice. Always check conditions with a local operator before you set out.

How much does it cost to visit the Sótano de las Huahuas in 2026?

Admission to the Sótano de las Huahuas is $60 MXN per person; on top of that, local guides charge between $200 and $350 MXN per person, depending on group size and whether transportation from Aquismón is included. Payment is cash only; there are no banks or digital payments in the area. We recommend bringing at least $600 MXN per person to cover the guide, a tip and anything unexpected along the way.

If you plan to do both sinkholes on the same trip, check our guide to how much it costs to visit the Huasteca Potosina in 2026 to put together a realistic budget that includes lodging, food and transportation from Ciudad Valles or Xilitla.

Tips before visiting either sinkhole

Both the Sótano de las Golondrinas and the Sótano de las Huahuas call for some basic preparation that many travelers underestimate. These aren't extreme adventure outings, but they aren't city-park strolls either: the walk in, the predawn start and the uneven ground call for the right gear and the right attitude. These are the five points we treat as mandatory for the groups we take.

  • Bring cash only: Neither community accepts cards or bank transfers. Withdraw money before leaving Ciudad Valles or Xilitla; the recommended minimum is $500 MXN per person for the Sótano de las Golondrinas and $600 MXN if you add the Huahuas.
  • Check the weather the night before: If there's rain or a cold front, the birds don't come out. Check the SMN (Mexico's national weather service) app or ask the community guide directly. Also see our guide to the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina to choose your dates well.
  • Book your guide ahead of time: The Unión de Guadalupe ejido controls access to the Sótano de las Golondrinas. In high season (July–October), guides sell out. Camping inside the ejido costs an extra $40 MXN per person, with prior permission.
  • Essential basic gear: A headlamp with a charged battery, layers, closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles and a poncho or light rain jacket. Check the packing checklist for the Potosí jungle before you pack.
  • Respect the communities' schedules: Access opens at 4:00 a.m. and guides don't wait. Leaving your lodging late means missing the birds' flight, which is the heart of the whole experience at the Sótano de las Golondrinas.

How do you get to the Sótano de las Golondrinas from Ciudad Valles?

Ciudad Valles is the most common starting point for travelers coming from central or northeastern Mexico. From there, the drive to the Sótano de las Golondrinas takes about 1 h 15 min under normal conditions. The groups we organize in the region usually leave Ciudad Valles at 3:00 a.m. to reach the rim before the flight begins. According to certified local guides, this is the only way to secure a spot at the lookout without rushing down the trail in the dark.

Driving your own car: distances and road conditions

From Ciudad Valles, take Federal Highway 85 toward Aquismón; past the town, the route turns into a dirt road for the last 4–6 km to the ejido entrance. In the dry season (November–May), a vehicle with good ground clearance is enough. In the rainy season, a 4x4 truck is recommended, or you can hire local transportation directly in Aquismón. Shared transportation (colectivo) from Ciudad Valles to Aquismón costs around $60–$80 MXN per person. From Xilitla the trip is longer (about 2.5 hours), so in that case it's best to arrive the night before: the ejido allows camping with prior permission.

Can you do it as a day trip from Xilitla?

Yes, but it takes a tight itinerary. Leaving Xilitla before 2:30 a.m. gets you to the rim in time for the flight. Some travelers choose to spend the night before in Aquismón to take the stress out of the predawn drive. If Xilitla is your base and you want to make the most of your time, combine the Sótano de las Golondrinas with the region's waterfalls. Read our guide to 3 days in the Huasteca Potosina for an itinerary that covers both areas without sacrificing either.

Frequently asked questions about the Sótano de las Golondrinas

What time do the birds fly out of the Sótano de las Golondrinas?

The birds fly out around 5:00 a.m. in summer and around 6:00 a.m. in winter. If it rains or the temperature drops sharply, they don't come out that day. In 2026, we recommend reaching the rim at least 40 minutes before the estimated time.

How much is admission to the Sótano de las Golondrinas in 2026?

Admission to the Sótano de las Golondrinas is $100 MXN per person. Camping inside the ejido costs an extra $40 MXN. Cash only; bring at least $500 MXN per person.

How do you get to the Sótano de las Golondrinas from Ciudad Valles?

Take Federal Highway 85 toward Aquismón, a drive of about 1 h 15 min. The last 4–6 km are dirt road. In the rainy season, a high-clearance vehicle or a 4x4 truck is recommended. You need to leave before 3:00 a.m. to get there in time for the birds' flight.

Is the Sótano de las Golondrinas safe for families or couples?

Yes, as long as you go with an authorized community guide and basic gear. The trail to the rim is moderate, and families with children 8 and older walk it. In the Huasteca Potosina, the local ejidos make sure access is safe. For couples, pair it with a stay in Xilitla: see our guide to a romantic getaway in Xilitla.

Can you camp near the Sótano de las Golondrinas?

Yes. The Unión de Guadalupe ejido allows camping on its land with prior permission. It costs an extra $40 MXN per person on top of the regular admission. Staying overnight at the ejido is the best option for people coming from far away: you don't have to leave Ciudad Valles or Xilitla in the middle of the night, and you get to see both the dawn flight out and the dusk return on the same day.
